# Regions

This folder contains the five administrative regions of Denmark as tracked by the national Acute Surgery Database (AKDB). Each page details a specific region's clinical quality indicator performance—such as timely antibiotic administration, rapid surgical intervention for life-threatening conditions, and 30-day mortality rates for patients with varying comorbidity scores. The pages also catalog the constituent hospitals operating within each region and provide demographic baseline comparisons to contextualize regional outcome disparities.

## Pages

- [[hovedstaden|Hovedstaden]] — The Capital Region, detailing its clinical indicator compliance, 30-day mortality rates, and constituent hospitals like Rigshospitalet and Amager og Hvidovre Hospital.
- [[midtjylland|Midtjylland]] — Central Denmark Region, covering its performance on acute surgical metrics, including rapid intervention times for life-threatening conditions and facilities like Aarhus Universitetshospital.
- [[nordjylland|Nordjylland]] — North Denmark Region, tracking its antibiotic administration rates, surgical intervention speeds, and mortality outcomes driven by facilities like Aalborg Universitetshospital.
- [[sjaelland|Sjælland]] — Region Zealand, outlining its fulfillment proportions for key quality indicators and major medical facilities like Sjællands Universitetshospital and Holbæk Sygehus.
- [[syddanmark|Syddanmark]] — Region of Southern Denmark, highlighting its significant deviations from national standards on early antibiotic treatment and nutritional assessment, alongside monitored facilities like Odense Universitetshospital.
